claims.text: Doped perovskite SrTiO3 can be engineered to form nanoscale short-range-ordered precipitates.
Nanoscale SRO precipitates in SrTiO3 will reduce lattice thermal conductivity by enhancing phonon scattering.
Undoped, stoichiometric SrTiO3 has a regular perovskite lattice structure.
Undoped, stoichiometric SrTiO3 exhibits negligible electronic conduction.
Controlled dopant introduction can induce nanoscale SRO precipitates within an SrTiO3 matrix.
Phonon-phonon and phonon-defect scattering dominate thermal transport from ambient to moderately elevated temperatures in the proposed SrTiO3 samples.
Precise control of dopant concentration and thermal processing can ensure a uniform distribution of SRO precipitates.
The relevant structural mediator is nanoscale SRO precipitates embedded in the insulating perovskite lattice.
SRO precipitates act as phonon-scattering centers.
Scattering by SRO precipitates reduces effective phonon scattering times.
Reduced phonon scattering times lead to decreased lattice thermal conductivity.
Doped SrTiO3 containing SRO precipitates will have measurably lower lattice thermal conductivity than undoped homogeneous SrTiO3.
Thermal conduction in the undoped homogeneous SrTiO3 baseline is dominated solely by lattice vibrations.
Maximum dopant solubility may limit the proposed effect.
Very high dopant concentrations may cause structural instability.
At very high temperatures, conduction mechanisms other than lattice heat transport may become significant.
The quantitative relationship between SRO precipitate density or size and phonon scattering time is not precisely known.
TEM can be used to verify the formation, size, and distribution of the proposed SRO precipitates.
TDTR can be used to compare thermal conductivity across the proposed sample series and temperature range.
